title: Kavinsky, OutRun (album cover)
lede: The cover of Kavinsky’s 2013 album: a red Ferrari Testarossa with its headlights on and a man in silhouette under lightning, with a red-and-blue brush-script name.
summary: Red Testarossa, palm silhouette, lightning, red-and-blue script “Kavinsky”. Album cover, 2013.

creator.name: Charlotte Delarue (art direction); The Directors Bureau Special Projects (design concept, photography)

evidence.note: Inspected the 1200 px front-cover image from the [Cover Art Archive](https://musicbrainz.org/release/e07d3a7a-e3e4-4786-b758-27715e830652/cover-art) in a scratch folder. Not stored. Credits are from the [Discogs record of the US CD](https://www.discogs.com/release/4384034-Kavinsky-OutRun) (Record Makers, Casablanca, Republic, B0018156-02).

styles.note: The album that named the Outrun look after the 1986 Sega game: a Testarossa, palms, a night sky, and a neon brush-script logotype.

context: Wikipedia: the album was “released on 22 February 2013 by Record Makers, Vertigo Records and Mercury Records” and is “named after Sega’s 1986 arcade game of the same name, which featured the Ferrari Testarossa.” The cover shows “a red Ferrari Testarossa with its headlights on, and a silhouette of a man with clouds behind them.” [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OutRun_(album)).

Wikipedia: Kavinsky’s backstory is of a young man who crashed his Testarossa in 1986 and came back in 2006 as a zombie who makes electronic music, and the visual style draws on 1980s video games, *Miami Vice*, and the films of Dario Argento.

Discogs credits art direction to Charlotte Delarue, the design concept and photography to The Directors Bureau Special Projects, image manipulation to Adrien Blanchat, and the film stills to director Marcus Herring. [Discogs](https://www.discogs.com/release/4384034-Kavinsky-OutRun).
The [synthwave](style:synthwave) record cites PC Gamer: the Testarossa and palm trees on this cover reference the game.
observed: Black bands fill the top and bottom quarters, so the picture reads as a wide letterboxed film frame across the middle.
The frame is a misty blue night: a palm tree and dark foliage at the left, white forked lightning at the upper right.
A red Ferrari Testarossa sits low across the centre with one headlight on and a beam of light to the right. A man in a jacket stands in silhouette at the right.
“Kavinsky” runs across the upper left in a red, dry-brush script with a blue offset shadow. “OUTRUN” sits under it in small, widely spaced pale capitals.
There is no grid, no sun, and no chrome type.
interpretation: This is the photographic, cinematic branch of the style: the car, the palm, and the night carry the period, and a neon-like script carries the logo. It shows that the grid and the sun are not required when the car and the script are present.
borrow: Letterbox a hero image between black bands to make it read as a film still.
Pair a fast brush-script name with a small, widely tracked capital subtitle.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The cover art is in copyright (Record Makers and Republic Records, 2013).
